intro: AMF to STL converts 3D models from AMF to STL on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to print an AMF on a printer or slicer that only accepts STL. STL is the format every slicer reads (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer): it only stores triangles, with no units or colours.

AMF (ISO/ASTM 52915) is the additive manufacturing XML format: it stores units, several parts, coloured materials and copies of one object, and PrusaSlicer and Cura open it. AMF and STL both use the Z axis up, like 3D printing, so the model is not turned; the AMF's units are read from the file and you can choose those of the STL.

You can apply a scale, choose the original's units if the AMF does not store them and decide what to do with the parts: keep them separate inside the STL when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The AMF geometry reaches the STL without being simplified or repaired. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task; they are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted when they expire.
steps: Upload one or more AMF files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the STL come out rotated or on its side?
faq.a: Because AMF and STL may use different axes. Try ticking or unticking “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
The AMF material colours go into the STL if the format supports them; STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the model has holes?
faq.a: The STL has the same geometry as the AMF. To close them before printing, use Repair STL.
